thread.title: Cannabis company MedMen taps Apple, Forever 21 veteran as CFO

author: I-Chun Chen
title: Cannabis company MedMen taps Apple, Forever 21 veteran as CFO

organizations.name: pst cannabis company medmen enterprises inc.

text: – Correspondent, L.A. Biz Dec 7, 2018, 2:19pm PST Cannabis company MedMen Enterprises Inc. has hired Michael Kramer, a finance executive who has worked at retailers such as Apple Inc., Abercrombie & Fitch and Forever 21, as its chief financial officer, effective Dec. 10. Los Angeles-based MedMen (OTCQX: MMNFF; CSE: MMEN; FSE: A2JM6N) said interim CFO Jim Miller will return to his previous role as the company’s vice president of accounting. “Michael’s extensive financial and operational experience in retail and tech, and his success in scaling high-growth businesses will be instrumental as MedMen moves to operationalize the balance of our footprint,” MedMen co-founder and Chief Executive Adam Bierman said in a statement. “His appointment underscores our commitment to investing in a strong management team with a track record of execution. Our industry and business continue to evolve, and it is paramount that we have the right talent to execute at each stage of our growth.” Kramer’s three decades of experience include serving as CFO of Apple Retail, where he developed brick-and-mortar retail strategies. He also was an executive at Abercrombie & Fitch, where he oversaw 12 quarters of increased year-over-year earnings, according to MedMen. In addition, Kramer has been on advisory boards at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania and Kansas State University’s Business School. “I look forward to working with MedMen’s talented team to advance its growth plan,” Kramer said. “We will remain focused on execution, on maintaining a strong balance sheet and moving toward profitability.” Kramer’s hiring follows a number of key executive hires by MedMen in recent months, including Chief Operating Officer Ben Cook , previously with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) and Sam’s Club; Chief Marketing Officer David H. Dancer , a veteran marketing executive with more than 25 years of experience at companies such as Teleflora, Charles Schwab, Visa and American Express; and Chief Digital Officer Mike Lane, who has worked at Live Nation, Ticketmaster, Fox Broadcasting and Adobe. In November, MedMen reported a fiscal first-quarter loss of $12.5 million, compared with a loss of $5.3 million in the year-ago period. Revenue, however, jumped to $21.5 million from $1.8 million.
